questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 12 cm. What is its total surface area? (use π ≈ 3.14, round to 1 decimal place)
questions.why: Total surface area = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2(3.14)(16) + 2(3.14)(4)(12) = 100.5 + 301.4 = 401.9 cm². A common mistake is forgetting the two circular ends (giving 301.4) or only using one end.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic's parliament used a voting system called proportional representation. What problem did this cause?
options: It made it hard for any single party to win a majority, leading to unstable coalition governments
It banned smaller parties from standing in elections
It gave the army automatic control of parliament
It meant only wealthy landowners could vote
questions.answer: It made it hard for any single party to win a majority, leading to unstable coalition governments
questions.why: Proportional representation gave even small parties seats, so no single party could easily govern alone — this led to many short-lived, unstable coalition governments in Weimar Germany.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: By 1932, unemployment in Germany had reached around 6 million. Which best explains why this specifically boosted support for the Nazis rather than other parties?
options: The Nazis promised strong leadership, jobs, and national revival, directly targeting people's fears and frustrations
The Nazis were the only legal political party allowed to campaign
Unemployed workers were forced by law to join the Nazi Party
The Nazis controlled all German newspapers by 1932
questions.answer: The Nazis promised strong leadership, jobs, and national revival, directly targeting people's fears and frustrations
questions.why: It's not enough that unemployment rose — the Nazis specifically offered clear, confident solutions (jobs, strong government, national pride) that spoke directly to desperate voters, winning support away from other parties.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: After WWII, Australia actively recruited migrants from Europe under schemes like 'Populate or Perish', while also needing labour for its expanding industries. Which best explains why the government saw migration as urgent, not just useful?
options: Australia feared it was underpopulated and vulnerable, so migration was tied to both economic growth and national security
Australia had no unemployment problem and needed migrants purely for variety
Migration was only about filling university places
The government wanted to reduce the population of cities
questions.answer: Australia feared it was underpopulated and vulnerable, so migration was tied to both economic growth and national security
questions.why: 'Populate or Perish' reflected genuine fear that a small population left Australia exposed after WWII, so migration served both economic (labour) and strategic (defence) purposes at once — not just convenience.

questions.subject: Commerce
questions.prompt: A student is writing a business plan for a new gym and wants to include a SWOT analysis. Which best describes what a SWOT analysis actually examines?
options: The business's own Strengths and Weaknesses, alongside external Opportunities and Threats
A summary of competitor prices and customer numbers in the market
A one-page overview of the entire business plan
A list of the products and services the business will sell
questions.answer: The business's own Strengths and Weaknesses, alongside external Opportunities and Threats
questions.why: SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats — it looks at internal factors (S/W) and external factors (O/T) about the business itself, not general market data like prices or foot traffic, which belongs in market analysis.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: White blood cells called phagocytes respond to infection by engulfing and digesting pathogens. What is this process called?
options: Phagocytosis
Antibody production
Vaccination
Inflammation
questions.why: Phagocytosis is when phagocytes engulf and break down pathogens directly — this is different from antibody production, which is done by lymphocytes and targets specific pathogens.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.prompt: A small country town loses young people as they move to Sydney for university and jobs, while the city's population keeps growing. What is this movement of people within the same country called?
options: Internal migration
International migration
Urbanisation
Immigration
questions.why: Movement of people within the same country (town to city) is internal migration. Urbanisation describes the overall growth of city populations as a trend, not the individual movement itself, and immigration/international migration involve crossing borders.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 11 cm and a height of 6 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?
options: 33 cm²
66 cm²
17 cm²
34 cm²
questions.why: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 11 × 6 = 33 cm². Rushing often causes forgetting the ½, giving 66 cm² — always halve after multiplying base and height.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A rectangular prism (cuboid) has length 5 cm, width 4 cm, and height 3 cm. What is its total surface area?
options: 94 cm²
60 cm²
47 cm²
120 cm²
questions.why: Surface area = 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(20 + 15 + 12) = 2(47) = 94 cm². A common error is finding only half the surface (47 cm²) by forgetting to double, or confusing surface area with volume (60 cm³).

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: The Weimar Republic relied heavily on Article 48, which allowed the President to rule by emergency decree without parliament's approval. Why was this significant?
options: It showed a built-in weakness where democracy could be bypassed in a crisis, which later helped Hitler seize power legally
It guaranteed that parliament always had final control over all laws
It gave ordinary citizens the power to overrule the President
It abolished the position of Chancellor entirely
questions.answer: It showed a built-in weakness where democracy could be bypassed in a crisis, which later helped Hitler seize power legally
questions.why: Article 48 let the president rule without parliament during emergencies — a democratic loophole that Hitler and Hindenburg later used to erode democracy from within, rather than overthrowing it by force.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why the Great Depression specifically strengthened Hitler's appeal, rather than simply making all politicians equally unpopular?
options: Hitler offered simple explanations and confident promises of recovery, while other parties seemed divided and indecisive
The Great Depression only affected supporters of the Nazi Party
All other political parties disappeared once the Depression began
The Depression had no real effect on how people voted
questions.answer: Hitler offered simple explanations and confident promises of recovery, while other parties seemed divided and indecisive
questions.why: It's not just that people were angry — Hitler stood out by offering clear scapegoats and bold solutions when other parties looked weak and quarrelling, which is why his support specifically grew.
